name: @hydranium/data-server
description: Typed-RPC protocol head for the hydranium framework. Peer of @hydranium/core/lsp and @hydranium/glsp-server; built on @hydranium/core.

scripts.prepack: node -e "const m=require('./package.json'),fs=require('node:fs');const missing=[m.main,...Object.values(m.bin||{})].filter(entry=>entry&&!fs.existsSync(entry));if(missing.length){console.error('prepack '+m.name+': not built ('+missing.join(', ')+' missing). Run the build before packing: a files entry that matches nothing is skipped silently, so the tarball would ship src only.');process.exit(1);}"

//browser: Selects the diagnostics default per platform, the same mechanism @eclipse-glsp/server uses to swap its node build for its browser one. The Node module imports @hydranium/core/node; a browser bundler resolves the twin instead and therefore never follows that import, which is what keeps this package's `.` entry bundleable. Node ignores this field, so a Node host keeps the real implementation with no configuration. `check:neutral` is the proof it still applies — it bundles `.` for the browser and would fail on node:fs the moment the mapping stops matching.
//peerDependencies: `vscode-jsonrpc` takes a caret, so the framework shares the transport the LSP connection resolves, which an `init` scaffold pins: each `vscode-languageserver-protocol` release pins its transport exactly, so an exact peer would name a copy a fresh install rarely holds. The caret excludes 8.x, so a tree whose top holds GLSP's copy fails the peer with a named ERESOLVE warning, an error under `--strict-peer-deps`, rather than resolving silently. No peer reaches a NESTED copy, such as GLSP's or one the LSP packages nest; docs/adopting/requirements.md has the chain. The wire compares message types and `ResponseError`s by copy identity, so the framework sends typed messages by method name and recognises errors with `isResponseError` rather than `instanceof`.
//prepack: The publish guard, a `prepack` rather than a `prepare`: `prepack` runs only when a tarball is made (`npm pack`, `npm publish`) and never on install, so it cannot break the install it has no business touching. What it defends against: `files` lists `lib`, `lib` is gitignored, and a `files` entry matching nothing is skipped SILENTLY — so `npm publish` from an unbuilt tree emits a tarball of `src` and nothing else, with no error.
